instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Initial interpretation of the walk-in's partial manifest and generic container photograph
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Ambiguous documentary and photographic evidence was perceived as a clear match to a pre-existing shipment-pattern template despite its generic/partial nature and available time to authenticate.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is related to perceptual pattern-matching but is not an approved equivalent of Perceptual Bias. The occurrence has the right initial-document location and captures the clear-match interpretation, but the strict target label is absent.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The stated mechanism and quote capture ambiguous physical evidence being read as a textbook pattern match and the routine-shipment alternative being discounted, which fully matches cb_01's evidence-interpretation operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: All quoted material is present in the interview and attributed to the Participant. The label is broader/adjacent to the hidden target; no quotation is fabricated.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Relief at a possible breakthrough and the resulting validation pace
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Desire for the walk-in to be genuine because it would validate months of effort inflates confidence in source veracity, independently of evidence and deadline pressure.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Affect heuristic is a related affect-based judgment construct, but it is not equivalent to motivational wishful thinking.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The quote directly links relief to faster movement toward validation. The RAG further infers that affect served as a cue to credibility, but the interview does not clearly state that desire inflated source-veracity confidence; this is only a partial match to cb_02.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quotation is verbatim and correctly attributed. The asserted credibility/urgency inference is stronger than the participant's explicit statement, which links relief to pace.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Evaluation of the walk-in's claimed logistics background as an explanation for access
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The access-explanation argument was accepted because its conclusion fit the network narrative, with an explicit asymmetric evidentiary standard, rather than being assessed on the inference's validity.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: No RAG finding was assigned to this hidden instance after one-to-one matching; obs_003 was assigned to cb_04 because its primary mechanism and narrative-weighting evidence fit that segment more strongly.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The raw interview contains the asymmetric-standard cue, but a single RAG occurrence cannot be credited twice. No separately localized RAG occurrence remains for cb_03.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: No supporting RAG occurrence was matched to this instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Drafting the report while reconciling corroborating sub-source material with the technical port discrepancy
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Corroborating evidence received disproportionate narrative space while a genuinely contradictory technical item was reduced to a footnote despite ample time to reconcile it.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a related evidence-evaluation construct, not an approved equivalent of Selective Attention Bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The occurrence specifically states that the contradictory technical flag was footnoted, corroborating material received most narrative space, and no evidentiary or scheduling reason justified the disparity. This fully matches cb_04's attention/weighting operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The supporting footnote/narrative-space quotation is verbatim and correctly attributed. A separate quoted access-claim rationale also touches cb_03, but the occurrence is scored once at its primary evidence-weighting location.

instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The singular/plural wording is the same target construct; no alias expansion is needed.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate quote describes the wording choice changing perceived actionability and caveat use while the underlying estimate stayed constant, fully matching cb_05. It qualifies only at the candidate-inclusive fourth threshold.

main_failure_modes: The identified findings use confirmation bias for two distinct hidden mechanisms, so strict label-plus-mechanism scoring rejects both even though their mechanisms align.
The relief finding uses affect heuristic, but the transcript supports faster validation more clearly than the hidden wishful-thinking requirement of inflated source-veracity confidence.
The access-claim belief-bias instance is not separately matched; obs_003 is assigned once to the stronger report-weighting match at seg_004.
The framing-effects finding is left at candidate status, so it does not count until the candidate-inclusive threshold.
main_strengths: The high-confidence planning-fallacy finding is an exact label, quote, location, and mechanism match.
The moderate-confidence authority-bias finding also fully matches its hidden target.
Mechanism-first scoring recognizes the initial perceptual pattern-match and the selective-attention treatment of the port discrepancy.
Both candidates use valid interview quotations, and cand_002 is a full candidate-tier match.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run is substantially better at finding biased segments and matching mechanisms than at assigning the benchmark's target labels. The candidate tier adds useful coverage of framing, while also exposing duplicate speculation around the initial evidence. These are per-interview results and do not support dataset-level comparisons or significance claims.
